content.influenza_vaccination: An annual influenza vaccination in patients with stable ASCVD appears to be associated with reduced incidence of MI, an improved prognosis in patients with HF, and decreased CV risk in adults aged 65 years and older. Influenza vaccination given early after an MI or in high-risk CAD has been shown to result in a lower risk of all-cause death and CV death at 12 months. Influenza vaccination is recommended for all ACS patients and should be given preferentially during index hospitalization during influenza season for those not protected by a seasonal influenza vaccination.
content.13.3.9_Anti-inflammatory_drugs: Inflammation plays a central role in the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis and acute coronary events. Recent trials tested the anti-inflammatory agent colchicine in acute and chronic coronary syndromes. In the Colchicine Cardiovascular Outcomes Trial (COLCOT), low-dose colchicine (0.5 mg daily) in 4745 patients with a recent ACS was associated with a significant reduction of the primary composite endpoint (CV death, resuscitated cardiac arrest, MI, stroke, or urgent revascularization) versus placebo; pneumonia was more frequent in the colchicine group. The Low-dose Colchicine trial-2 (LoDoCo2) enrolled 5522 patients with CCS (84% with prior ACS) randomized to colchicine (0.5 mg daily) or placebo; the primary composite endpoint rate was significantly lower in the colchicine group, though non-CV death incidence was higher. Benefits of colchicine in reducing CV events were consistent irrespective of history and timing of prior ACS.
